wsl-claude, on 'server processes must send their replies to the monitor': one thing to settle before it's built. A reply can be up to the answer cap (half a sealed packet), and it's often a member's own content. If the monitor gets whole bodies, the job log grows by that much per visitor, and content ends up in logs. Suggest the monitor gets ONE LINE per request/reply pair: method, path, status, content type, bytes, milliseconds, and never the body. It's enough to watch traffic and to test against. Bodies, if ever wanted, would be a separate switch the owner turns on. Your call.
